Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 53, "heading": "CHAPTER 51. THE BEGINNING OF A LONGER JOURNEY", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u053-b0089", "target": "По этому знаку маленький слон с ловкостью, почти чудесной для такого крохотного животного, развернул кресло вместе с мистером Омером и, грохоча, влетел в гостиную очертя голову, не задев дверного косяка; мистер Омер несказанно наслаждался представлением и оглядывался на меня по дороге с таким видом, словно это было торжествующим итогом всех трудов его жизни.", "source_sha256": "b733abe2005d1d2ec969fe89c66ce0f4d6aabf6008de5a9ce32d3d1e1264e6dd", "target_id": "ru-en85-u053-b0089", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "ed370d5e6f5b021cfbdeb1e2703cbce96d67c5b35b088348cf55f52f10c2ae06"}, {"source_id": "en85-u053-b0090", "target": "Побродив по городу, я пошёл к дому Хэма. Пегготи теперь окончательно переселилась сюда, а свой дом сдала преемнику мистера Баркиса по извозному делу, который хорошо ей заплатил за доброе имя, повозку и лошадь. Кажется, та самая медлительная лошадь, на которой ездил мистер Баркис, всё ещё работала.", "source_sha256": "fe34399cd407f03708d04f72282e1538e55c36deac862c9d5985848735e683a0", "target_id": "ru-en85-u053-b0090", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "a6e9b17232a253bad7ccbed05d625b294bb58a1e7ca2716f923fc18f925c4ad5"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 51, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u053-b0091", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I found them in the neat kitchen, accompanied by Mrs. Gummidge, who had been fetched from the old boat by Mr. Peggotty himself. I doubt if she could have been induced to desert her post, by anyone else. He had evidently told them all. Both Peggotty and Mrs. Gummidge had their aprons to their eyes, and Ham had just stepped out ‘to take a turn on the beach’. He presently came home, very glad to see me; and I hope they were all the better for my being there. We spoke, with some approach to cheerfulness, of Mr. Peggotty’s growing rich in a new country, and of the wonders he would describe in his letters. We said nothing of Emily by name, but distantly referred to her more than once. Ham was the serenest of the party.", "sha256": "d6817783be15947db7617d9f493d104b519262d40e0499cd2871ff09663c7afa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[92]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0092", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But, Peggotty told me, when she lighted me to a little chamber where the Crocodile book was lying ready for me on the table, that he always was the same. She believed (she told me, crying) that he was broken-hearted; though he was as full of courage as of sweetness, and worked harder and better than any boat-builder in any yard in all that part. There were times, she said, of an evening, when he talked of their old life in the boat-house; and then he mentioned Emily as a child. But, he never mentioned her as a woman.", "sha256": "e2f3634c3bfec9a7e2563ef76f5872d39a86391973fb47e3a17b55b625fef966", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[93]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I thought I had read in his face that he would like to speak to me alone. I therefore resolved to put myself in his way next evening, as he came home from his work. Having settled this with myself, I fell asleep. That night, for the first time in all those many nights, the candle was taken out of the window, Mr. Peggotty swung in his old hammock in the old boat, and the wind murmured with the old sound round his head.", "sha256": "83623a263318f477c136688b5b0a574bdc55dd566c2020046b70c1e2c2cd210b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[94]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0094", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "All next day, he was occupied in disposing of his fishing-boat and tackle; in packing up, and sending to London by waggon, such of his little domestic possessions as he thought would be useful to him; and in parting with the rest, or bestowing them on Mrs. Gummidge. She was with him all day. As I had a sorrowful wish to see the old place once more, before it was locked up, I engaged to meet them there in the evening. But I so arranged it, as that I should meet Ham first.", "sha256": "67b5fa720d99bfdb1b38b2659cd48b34896e62126644228d5af3cb072cd8ca92", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[95]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0095", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was easy to come in his way, as I knew where he worked. I met him at a retired part of the sands, which I knew he would cross, and turned back with him, that he might have leisure to speak to me if he really wished. I had not mistaken the expression of his face. We had walked but a little way together, when he said, without looking at me:", "sha256": "0a6251e0967797361f4b1d2d7659d00709e514233b0fc0ac7c0fad641f21e71a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[96]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0096", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mas’r Davy, have you seen her?’", "sha256": "524238b612819102ce5ad94f7473951113f0206c43ab9b00a07952de6ba40848", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[97]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0097", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Only for a moment, when she was in a swoon,’ I softly answered.", "sha256": "e12f1d464e452b67e92163d73eaf72111b9e5ca3a60ecfdcdbf4164a48e65b19", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[98]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0098", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We walked a little farther, and he said:", "sha256": "003df75e56854188881df2b7aa1b21a58e81fb3f0d95d9a75553cc8ec58f9511", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[99]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0099", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mas’r Davy, shall you see her, d’ye think?’", "sha256": "b8f3ad79a8f31cd059ef3aea09b63b4549e049330682edbecf922366a0037b7d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[100]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0100", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It would be too painful to her, perhaps,’ said I.", "sha256": "b07b190fbed3c19f614a1f2d80f33e9a08dd480a96b0c71f5952ef4c90f781c7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[101]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0101", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have thowt of that,’ he replied. ‘So ‘twould, sir, so ‘twould.’", "sha256": "3ec6fe8a667014adaac718aa7ba70ec0cdfff64538f27ea274bdd62b04c06e93", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[102]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0102", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘But, Ham,’ said I, gently, ‘if there is anything that I could write to her, for you, in case I could not tell it; if there is anything you would wish to make known to her through me; I should consider it a sacred trust.’", "sha256": "e1b691ce680dc31baf7745c4b333e288cc0ec7ba74acf3bcd77b806e3199bc3a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[103]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0103", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am sure on’t. I thankee, sir, most kind! I think theer is something I could wish said or wrote.’", "sha256": "002e00be57cef3ba26510ec230c0e8c50fd8e0e7d568635eecb27aaca82f15af", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[104]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0104", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘What is it?’", "sha256": "9288a210f990abfdb2c850cd6e7b9b6c1c410eec07ba89917131a70f27939ee1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[105]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0105", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We walked a little farther in silence, and then he spoke.", "sha256": "7c9d02b61c293cd54e7121d8be5f00a17e8d6e532f99bfd4c4252a8b39c2e8eb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[106]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0106", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘’Tan’t that I forgive her. ‘Tan’t that so much. ‘Tis more as I beg of her to forgive me, for having pressed my affections upon her. Odd times, I think that if I hadn’t had her promise fur to marry me, sir, she was that trustful of me, in a friendly way, that she’d have told me what was struggling in her mind, and would have counselled with me, and I might have saved her.’", "sha256": "766ec7538b77b7fc948f87c1c4d110d1b249806b6b327a023969638a4ebc9af1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[107]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0107", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I pressed his hand. ‘Is that all?’ ‘Theer’s yet a something else,’ he returned, ‘if I can say it, Mas’r Davy.’", "sha256": "b0335f86aa1cc8d0483a820df9024843ba161978a1e0ca0089ffc31f5300d053", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[108]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0108", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We walked on, farther than we had walked yet, before he spoke again. He was not crying when he made the pauses I shall express by lines. He was merely collecting himself to speak very plainly.", "sha256": "9c96899b680c8d1eb1fbdfcd08e3ecc7a5d647b21452d31c6107ec0549be55f7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[109]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0109", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I loved her—and I love the mem’ry of her—too deep—to be able to lead her to believe of my own self as I’m a happy man. I could only be happy—by forgetting of her—and I’m afeerd I couldn’t hardly bear as she should be told I done that. But if you, being so full of learning, Mas’r Davy, could think of anything to say as might bring her to believe I wasn’t greatly hurt: still loving of her, and mourning for her: anything as might bring her to believe as I was not tired of my life, and yet was hoping fur to see her without blame, wheer the wicked cease from troubling and the weary are at rest—anything as would ease her sorrowful mind, and yet not make her think as I could ever marry, or as ‘twas possible that anyone could ever be to me what she was—I should ask of you to say that—with my prayers for her—that was so dear.’", "sha256": "36e42bb07be93ded38f21aafd20acb359a6695865b64e26dd46af84408d2897b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[110]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0110", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I pressed his manly hand again, and told him I would charge myself to do this as well as I could.", "sha256": "1ac390d010d935fb31c5c28cb0bac2f4652a70cd541dc6ca44df198b12ff276e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[111]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0111", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I thankee, sir,’ he answered. ‘’Twas kind of you to meet me. ‘Twas kind of you to bear him company down. Mas’r Davy, I unnerstan’ very well, though my aunt will come to Lon’on afore they sail, and they’ll unite once more, that I am not like to see him agen. I fare to feel sure on’t. We doen’t say so, but so ‘twill be, and better so. The last you see on him—the very last—will you give him the lovingest duty and thanks of the orphan, as he was ever more than a father to?’", "sha256": "0f812348c2a408aa849ee66476c1b165b3b6dba29ec930222d77057047613f37", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[112]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0112", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This I also promised, faithfully.", "sha256": "07d9b187e858f6a8dbee372ba21dc22bd6424fb57e1a4fc15a9c2ea46b5405de", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[113]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0113", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I thankee agen, sir,’ he said, heartily shaking hands. ‘I know wheer you’re a-going. Good-bye!’", "sha256": "5ab818ab510a9ef13483c88492e5ce2a88da985a80bb8842ca12966f09feac82", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[114]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0114", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "With a slight wave of his hand, as though to explain to me that he could not enter the old place, he turned away. As I looked after his figure, crossing the waste in the moonlight, I saw him turn his face towards a strip of silvery light upon the sea, and pass on, looking at it, until he was a shadow in the distance.", "sha256": "66a26ebeb9e4723e477379a406cf0c1904b819a4d0354d7cbf5f157c96efdbb0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[115]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0115", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The door of the boat-house stood open when I approached; and, on entering, I found it emptied of all its furniture, saving one of the old lockers, on which Mrs. Gummidge, with a basket on her knee, was seated, looking at Mr. Peggotty. He leaned his elbow on the rough chimney-piece, and gazed upon a few expiring embers in the grate; but he raised his head, hopefully, on my coming in, and spoke in a cheery manner.", "sha256": "bf0945517c802b3b175571d1c129bbb41e0c292e83ccc803ef3ee6ce3da792cd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[116]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0116", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Come, according to promise, to bid farewell to ‘t, eh, Mas’r Davy?’ he said, taking up the candle. ‘Bare enough, now, an’t it?’ ‘Indeed you have made good use of the time,’ said I.", "sha256": "e38c99d9353812e999e8976a128e870017b84b64ad7b1b078bee675d6c7ee397", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[117]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0117", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, we have not been idle, sir. Missis Gummidge has worked like a—I doen’t know what Missis Gummidge an’t worked like,’ said Mr. Peggotty, looking at her, at a loss for a sufficiently approving simile.", "sha256": "7d8732d7600f5c207b1f05b24346ae966b2462269991bed779de1b271c1fd1ec", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[118]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0118", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mrs. Gummidge, leaning on her basket, made no observation.", "sha256": "e5ccaee5e1ae93bb32a07a12b0d8395d26d660e1a914ff3e2ac9d0d493ce447e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[119]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0119", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Theer’s the very locker that you used to sit on, ‘long with Em’ly!’ said Mr. Peggotty, in a whisper. ‘I’m a-going to carry it away with me, last of all. And heer’s your old little bedroom, see, Mas’r Davy! A’most as bleak tonight, as ‘art could wish!’", "sha256": "76e27d4d10c13d152cb819fa0cf670e9a4e5542dea34114fba66f8a05a3cb36e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[120]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0120", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "In truth, the wind, though it was low, had a solemn sound, and crept around the deserted house with a whispered wailing that was very mournful. Everything was gone, down to the little mirror with the oyster-shell frame. I thought of myself, lying here, when that first great change was being wrought at home. I thought of the blue-eyed child who had enchanted me. I thought of Steerforth: and a foolish, fearful fancy came upon me of his being near at hand, and liable to be met at any turn.", "sha256": "a0bd2489548ba94452e586c30a0df1f9bce22ad6eccf96362e7e76686ae6224a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[121]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0121", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘’Tis like to be long,’ said Mr. Peggotty, in a low voice, ‘afore the boat finds new tenants. They look upon ‘t, down heer, as being unfortunate now!’", "sha256": "4601183ea2aac014b75c9270e87dd9621d27e0300d82d9a18a396531d1d5f8f6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[122]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0122", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Does it belong to anybody in the neighbourhood?’ I asked.", "sha256": "2e6a71474729784c73b18de8745883dcea90a2a7853ece02fa034075ac1151ce", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[123]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
